$comment: Managed by copilot-governance. Do not edit this file downstream.
Surface: Copilot CLI and the Copilot cloud coding agent.
Deployed to .github/hooks/copilot-cli-interceptor.json.
Copilot CLI splits prompt submission across two events with very different
capabilities, which is why this surface needs its own registration rather
than reusing the VS Code one:
userPromptSubmitted   Notification only. The reference is explicit that
output is not processed; it cannot modify or block.
Registered purely so shadow-mode telemetry records
prompts on this surface. The engine recognises it as
notify-only via surfaces.json and returns {}.
userPromptTransformed Mutation only. modifiedTransformedPrompt replaces
the content the model receives and what is stored in
session history; the timeline still shows what the
developer typed, and the replacement is replayed
unchanged when a session resumes.
This is the ONLY surface with real, documented prompt replacement — so it is
the only place the hybrid strategy's rewrite arm executes literally. It is
also the only surface that CANNOT block: userPromptTransformed is
mutation-only, so an enforcing deny rule degrades here to a hard refusal
instruction written into the rewritten prompt. That is a real enforcement
gap and is documented as one in docs/prompt-interception-plan.md.
Copilot CLI uses per-shell command keys (bash / powershell) and timeoutSec,
unlike the VS Code schema's single command / timeout.
Non-zero exits other than 2 are logged and execution continues (fail-open),
which is the desired degradation if node is missing.
